newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower, but tone firms late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower, but tone firms late.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended lower, but the market's tone firmed slightly after most contracts crept steadily above session lows, traders said.
"It was a classic grind to the upside," one bond futures analyst said.

He said many market participants were befuddled by June T-bonds' rebound to the 107-15/32 level considering the higher-than-expected monthly increases in the U.S. March industrial production and capacity utilization numbers.
Several traders said futures edged off lows due to the active buying of bonds in the cash market.
One bond market source said the cash bond buying may have stemmed from mortgage companies with service exposure, and said the interest could be a short-term phenomenon.
"We are clearly on the defensive until the (April) employment reports," he said.
The U.S. monthly payrolls report is more than two weeks away.

On Thurday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, the U.S. February international trade report will be released. The U.S. trade deficit is forecast to narrow to $10.1 billion in February, from $12.71 billion in January.
U.S. weekly jobless claims will also be released at the same time. Claims are forecast to fall to 317,000 from 318,000 in the prior week.
"The capacity and production numbers increased more than we expected, and confirmed what we've been seeing with U.S. economic growth," one analyst said.

The numbers solidified expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise rates by 25 basis points -- and possibly 50 basis points -- at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in May.
On Monday, traders and dealers were speculating about the chance for a 50-basis-point tightening in May, but the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Tuesday dampened that talk.
"The CPI confirmed what we all knew -- that inflation is a phantom -- but today the pendulum swung to the idea that the Fed may be more decisive when they meet in May," he said.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were down 05/32 at 107-15/32, 10-year notes were off 03/32 at 105-22/32, munibonds were off 10/32 at 112-09/32, September T-bills were steady at 94.595 and September Eurodollars were down 0.005 at 93.705.
